newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Albright pays farewell call on U.N. chief Annan.
newsitem.headline: Albright pays farewell call on U.N. chief Annan.

text.p: American U.N. ambassador Madeleine Albright paid a farewell call on Tuesday on Secretary-General Kofi Annan, ending a four-year tour of duty at the United Nations.
Albright has been nominated by President Bill Clinton to succeed Warren Christopher as secretary of state and is awaiting confirmation by the U.S. Senate.
She will be succeeded as U.N. ambassador by Bill Richardson, a Democratic congressman from New Mexico who must also be confirmed by the Senate.
Albright's meeting with Annan, who took up his post as secretary-general on Jan. 1, included the subject of U.N. reform and related issues, according to U.N. and U.S. officials.
They also discussed a visit to Washington next week by Annan, who is to meet Clinton, Senate Foreign Relations Committee chairman Jesse Helms and other U.S. officials.
The United States owes the United Nations some $1.3 billion in budget dues and for peacekeeping operations.

A U.S. State Department source said earlier that Clinton intended proposing a repayment plan under which the United Nations would receive about $100 million in arrears this year. Another $900 million would be delayed until 1999, as leverage to ensure the carrying out of reforms.
Albright's U.N. deputy, Ambassador Edward Gnehm, will serve as charge d'affaires until Richardson takes up his post as U.S. permanent representative.
